questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a perfectly inelastic collision between two bodies, which quantity is conserved?
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved in every collision, but in an inelastic one the bodies stick together and part of the kinetic energy becomes heat and sound.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 5: Work, Energy and Power

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: White light splits into its constituent colours on passing through a prism because different colours have different:
options: Speeds in the glass, hence different refractive indices
questions.explanation: All colours travel at the same speed in vacuum, but in glass violet slows most, so it has the greatest refractive index and bends most, while red bends least.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 9: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 10 days. The fraction of the sample left undecayed after 30 days is:
questions.explanation: Thirty days is three half-lives, so the amount left is (1/2)³ = 1/8 of the original.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: Lithium resembles magnesium in many of its properties although they belong to different groups. This is known as:
questions.explanation: The first element of a group often resembles the second element of the next group because their ionic sizes and charge to radius ratios are close. Beryllium and aluminium form another such pair.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 3: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The acid catalysed hydrolysis of an ester in a large excess of water follows first order kinetics although two reactants are involved. Such a reaction is called:
questions.explanation: Water is present in such excess that its concentration hardly changes, so it merges into the rate constant and the reaction appears to depend only on the ester.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Loss of the biological activity of an enzyme on heating, without breaking its peptide bonds, is called:
questions.explanation: Heat and extreme pH break the hydrogen and other weak bonds that hold the secondary and tertiary structure, so the active site is lost while the primary structure survives.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Plants that flower only when the duration of light is less than a critical period are called:
questions.explanation: Short day plants such as chrysanthemum actually need a long uninterrupted dark period, and the stimulus is perceived by the leaves, not the buds.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 13: Plant Growth and Development

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The innermost layer of the microsporangium wall, which nourishes the developing pollen grains, is the:
questions.explanation: Tapetal cells are dense with cytoplasm and often have more than one nucleus, and they also supply the sporopollenin that builds the exine.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 1: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The volume of blood pumped out by each ventricle in one minute is called the:
questions.explanation: Cardiac output equals stroke volume times heart rate, roughly 70 mL × 72 per minute, which comes to about 5 litres in a healthy adult.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 15: Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: A woman who is a carrier of haemophilia marries a normal man. The probability that their son will be haemophilic is:
options: 25 percent of all children, that is half of the sons
Only the daughters will be affected
questions.explanation: The cross X^H X^h with X^H Y gives sons that are half normal and half haemophilic, so half the sons, which is a quarter of all the children, are affected.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
